end.summary:
Practised how visitors can harm fragile places through litter, noise, feeding animals, touching coral, and scratching historic carvings.
Identified responsible actions such as carrying rubbish back, keeping music low, avoiding carvings, and not walking on coral.
Explained some effects of noise, litter, feeding animals, and writing on historic walls.
The idea that many small actions add up to major harm or help was not yet established.
Feeding wild animals and the effect of one small wrapper remained mixed up at the end.
end.parentNote: Asha practised ways to protect beaches, wildlife, coral, and historic places. Tara gave examples such as carrying rubbish back, using earphones or keeping music low, and not touching or writing on carvings; explaining the effects helped them add details. Feeding animals was still seen as helpful when they look hungry, and the importance of one wrapper was not corrected by the end. At home, discuss one visit scenario and ask, “What could many visitors doing this do to the place?”
